(4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration.
